headline: IBM plans to install what it calls India's largest quantum computer at a new technology park in Amaravati in early 2027, according to the head of IBM in India.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: new today, a company executive's statement of plan; the source's own headline says 'first' while its text says 'largest'.
importance_line: Indian researchers and companies would gain local access to a large IBM quantum machine and a base for preparing their systems for post-quantum encryption, but the timing is one executive's statement of intent and the article gives no machine specifications or cost.
summary: The Economic Times reports that Sandip Patel, managing director of IBM India, said the Amaravati facility is "almost ready" and that machines should arrive early next year, part of IBM's Andhra Pradesh Quantum Valley project with Tata Consultancy Services and backed by chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu. Patel said real-world quantum applications are still three to five years away, so building uses for the machine, including preparing Indian companies for post-quantum cryptography, matters as much as the hardware.
